subtopic: FlashAttention / HBM traffic analysis of attention
learningObjective: Compare HBM traffic patterns between naive attention (materialized S = QK^T) and FlashAttention (block-tiled, streamed).
stem: Compare the HBM traffic of naive attention (which explicitly materializes S = QK^T in HBM before softmax and O = softmax(S)V) with FlashAttention over a single (B=1, H=1) head with sequence length N and head dim d = 64. Which comparison is correct?

options.text: Naive: O(N*d) reads/writes; FlashAttention: O(N^2) reads/writes. FlashAttention pays more HBM traffic in exchange for constant SMEM usage and lower peak register pressure.
Both algorithms have HBM traffic dominated by loading Q, K, V (O(N*d)) and writing O (O(N*d)); FlashAttention's benefit is entirely from fusing softmax into the matmul, not from I/O.
Both have HBM traffic O(N^2); FlashAttention only saves compute by fusing softmax with the K, V matmul into a single kernel.

Naive attention has HBM traffic dominated by writing and re-reading S (O(N^2)), on top of loading Q, K, V, and writing O. FlashAttention keeps S entirely on-chip and its HBM traffic is O(N^2 * d / M) where M is on-chip memory per SM, reducing to roughly O(N*d) when a full K/V tile fits — much less than naive for large N.

explanation: Naive attention materializes S = QK^T with shape [N, N] in HBM, so it incurs O(N^2) reads/writes for S (plus O(N*d) for Q, K, V, O). FlashAttention keeps S entirely on-chip: for a K/V tile of size B_c fitting in SMEM (size ~M), Q is streamed once per K/V tile, giving HBM I/O of O(N^2 * d / M). When M is large enough to hold K/V for the full computation, this collapses to O(N*d). The gap widens with N because the avoided O(N^2) S traffic scales quadratically.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: reverses the direction — naive is O(N^2), FA is much less.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: naive really does write/read S from HBM; that is the primary I/O cost.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: FLOP count is comparable; the win is I/O, not compute.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: FA's I/O is O(N^2 d / M), naive is Ω(N^2); FA wins as N grows.

assumptions: Standard (non-fused) baseline actually writes S to HBM (as in an unoptimized softmax-then-matmul kernel).
The on-chip memory M is at least large enough to hold one Q tile and one K/V tile.
nonImplications: Does not imply naive attention always materializes S; some implementations already fuse softmax with the S computation but still keep row-wise stats in HBM.
Does not imply that FLOP counts are equal in the backward pass; backward recomputation adds some FLOPs.

performanceClaim.scope: Asymptotic HBM traffic comparison of naive vs FlashAttention
